title: How to create a savings plan for major life events (wedding, baby, relocation)
description: Using 'Time-Bucketing' to fund multiple large goals simultaneously without debt.
content:
Life doesn't happen in a straight line; it happens in expensive clusters. You might need to pay for a wedding, a move across the country, and a new car all within 24 months. If you try to pay for these out of monthly cash flow, you will drown in credit card debt. The solution is **Time-Bucketing**. By breaking each goal into a monthly 'bill' you pay to yourself, you can smooth out the spikes in spending. This guide focuses on the logistics of managing competing savings priorities.

Key Takeaways

  • Define the 'Nut': You cannot save for 'a wedding.' You must save for a '$25,000 wedding in 18 months.' Specificity creates the math.
  • Separate Accounts: Do not lump all savings in one account. Use 'Sub-Savings' accounts (Buckets) or separate banks to prevent 'accidental borrowing' from the wrong fund.
  • Timeline Rules: Goals <2 years = Cash. Goals >5 years = Investing. Don't gamble your relocation fund on the stock market.
  • Prioritization: You likely can't fund everything fully. Rank them. Is the Wedding more important than the House Down Payment? Fund the #1 priority first.

Why It Matters (US Context)

The average US wedding is $30k. A cross-country move is $5k-$10k. First year of a baby is $15k+. These are 'Known Expenses.' Treating them as 'Emergencies' is a failure of planning.

The Parallel Processing Method

Let's assume you have $1,000/month available to save, but you have 3 goals.

The Goals

  • Wedding: Need $10,000 in 10 months. ($1,000/mo required).
  • New Car: Need $5,000 in 20 months. ($250/mo required).
  • Baby: Need $5,000 in 15 months. ($333/mo required).

Total Need: $1,583/month.

Actual Capacity: $1,000/month.

The Triage (Making it Work)

You have a $583 deficit. You have three choices:

  1. Push Dates: Move the Car purchase back to Month 30.
  2. Cut Scope: Reduce Wedding budget to $7,000.
  3. Increase Income: Pick up a side gig for 6 months.

Most people ignore the math and just charge the difference. Do not do this. Pick Option 2.

Where to Park the Cash

  1. Open a High-Yield Savings Account (HYSA): Use Ally or SoFi. They allow 'Vaults' or 'Buckets'.
  2. Create the Buckets: Label them clearly: 'Wedding Fund', 'Moving Fund'.
  3. Set Autopay: On payday, transfer $600 to Wedding, $200 to Car, $200 to Baby. Automation prevents you from spending it.
  4. Bonus Windfalls: Tax refunds and bonuses should be applied to the nearest goal to complete it faster.

Frequently Asked Questions

Should I invest my wedding fund?

No. If the market drops 20% right before the vendor payments are due, you are in trouble. Keep short-term goal money safe in HYSA or CDs.

What if an emergency happens?

Pause the goal savings. Divert the $1,000/mo to handle the emergency. The wedding might have to get smaller or later. This is better than going into debt.

How do I calculate relocation costs?

Budget for: Movers ($3-6k), First/Last Month Rent + Security Deposit ($4-6k), Travel ($1k), New Furniture ($2k). A standard move is easily $10k cash upfront.
